outcome: Postoperative pain scores (Visual Analogue Scale at 1h and 24h)
cohort: 100 patients aged 19-60 years undergoing gynaecological laparoscopic surgery who received propofol and rocuronium injections for anaesthesia induction.
finding: The occurrence of Propofol injection pain (PIP) and rocuronium-induced withdrawal movement (RIWM) during anaesthesia induction significantly predicted higher severity of postoperative pain and total opioid consumption, with RIWM being a stronger predictor than PIP.
